subject: Culture
title: Green Burial Movement
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Green Burial Movement.

hook.text: Traditional US burial uses 800,000 gallons of embalming fluid and 90,000 tons of steel per year.

buildup.text: Green burials skip embalming, use biodegradable caskets, and let the body decompose naturally.

discovery.text: Human composting is now legal in several US states. A body becomes soil in about 30 days.

twist.text: Green burial is actually the oldest method. Embalming only became standard during the US Civil War.

climax.text: How we handle the dead reflects what we believe about the earth. Green burial says we belong to it.

punchline.text: The newest burial trend is the oldest one.

quiz.question: When did embalming become standard practice in the United States?
